review_comments: looks like a random number. Why not 2.7s or 370ms?

it is a max timeout and is the same value is used on the other tests ... carrying over with current state ... if something keeps flaking here I will do a more thoroughly investigation, but right now it is blocking the CI

```
rep -r doer.Do ./staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/genericapiserver_graceful_termination_test.go | grep time

                        r = doer.Do(client, func(httptrace.GotConnInfo) {}, fmt.Sprintf("/echo?message=attempt-%d", i), time.Second)
                result := doer.Do(client, func(httptrace.GotConnInfo) {}, fmt.Sprintf("/echo?message=attempt-%d", i), 100*time.Millisecond)
```

having a subsecond timeout  for an http request is really a very low value
agreed… CI environments are often either underpowered or overloaded… subsecond timeouts are usually too tight tolerances

I'd recommend lengthening this to something like the normal 10 seconds if we're not making a request that we expect to hit the timeout. I don't see a benefit to making this a short timeout and maybe flaking on it.
